Title: Source 2: Agricultural Practices in the Americas
Content: This image shows a terrace and archeological ruins on a mountain near Cuzco in South America. Terraces are flat areas that look like steps in a set of stairs dug into the side of a hill or mountain. The Inca grew a variety of crops using terrace farming.
This drawing shows an Aztec chinampa. Chinampas are human-made islands built on a lake for agriculture. The Aztec used chinampas to grow many different crops.
This image, created in the late `text(1500s)`, shows Timucua men and women in a field preparing the soil and planting seeds. The Timucua people lived in the southeastern part of North America.
